content: 1. Chloramphenicol and Istradefylline: Chloramphenicol increases the plasma levels and effects of istradefylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Do not exceed 20 mg/day of istradefylline when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 2. Chloramphenicol and Ivacaftor: Chloramphenicol elevates ivacaftor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. 3. Chloramphenicol and Ivosidenib: Chloramphenicol significantly increases ivosidenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. Use alternative therapies. 4. Chloramphenicol and Ixabepilone: Chloramphenicol raises ixabepilone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 5. Chloramphenicol and Lapatinib: Chloramphenicol increases lapatinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative treatments. 6. Chloramphenicol and Larotrectinib: Chloramphenicol elevates larotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3–5 half-lives. 7. Chloramphenicol and Lefamulin: Chloramphenicol increases lefamulin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 8. Chloramphenicol and Lemborexant: Chloramphenicol raises lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Chloramphenicol and Leniolisib: Chloramphenicol increases leniolisib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 10. Chloramphenicol and Levamlodipine: Chloramphenicol elevates levamlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be required when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor for hypotension and edema. 11. Chloramphenicol and Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol: Chloramphenicol may reduce the efficacy of oral hormonal contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Chloramphenicol and Lomitapide: Chloramphenicol increases lomitapide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 13. Chloramphenicol and Lonafarnib: Chloramphenicol significantly increases lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Chloramphenicol and Lorlatinib: Chloramphenicol raises lorlatinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day and resume the original dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 15. Chloramphenicol and Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Chloramphenicol increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Chloramphenicol and Lurasidone: Chloramphenicol significantly increases lurasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Chloramphenicol and Maraviroc: Chloramphenicol elevates maraviroc levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily and monitor for toxicity. 18. Chloramphenicol and Mavacamten: Chloramphenicol increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting both CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure from systolic dysfunction. 19. Chloramphenicol and Midazolam: Chloramphenicol raises midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation. Monitor closely. 20. Chloramphenicol and Mifepristone: Chloramphenicol increases mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 21. Chloramphenicol and Montelukast: Chloramphenicol elevates montelukast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 22. Chloramphenicol and Nafcillin: Chloramphenicol reduces the efficacy of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely. 23. Chloramphenicol and Naloxegol: Chloramphenicol significantly increases naloxegol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Chloramphenicol and Nilotinib: Chloramphenicol raises nilotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 25. Chloramphenicol and Olaparib: Chloramphenicol increases olaparib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 26. Chloramphenicol and Oliceridine: Chloramphenicol elevates oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust oliceridine dosing and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 27. Chloramphenicol and Osilodrostat: Chloramphenicol increases osilodrostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Chloramphenicol and Pacritinib: Chloramphenicol significantly increases pacritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Chloramphenicol and Palbociclib: Chloramphenicol raises palbociclib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Chloramphenicol and Pazopanib: Chloramphenicol significantly increases pazopanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated.
